source.title: Promoting Exploration in Memory-Augmented Adam using Critical Momenta
source.authors: Pranshu Malviya; Gonçalo Mordido; A. Baratin; Reza Babanezhad Harikandeh; Jerry Huang; Simon Lacoste-Julien; Razvan Pascanu; A. P. Sarath Chandar

record.file_problem: none; full paper text including appendix is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own optimizer comparisons on held-out validation performance. On CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, its Adam baseline scores exceed the SGD results, challenging the broad direction of V4 in these tested settings; it does not directly compare Adam and SGD in the same table or setup.
record.gate_note: The paper compares optimizer validation results and measures sharpness, but sharpness results do not measure the training–test gap. Toy loss-surface results concern optimization loss and sharpness, not the claim versions' held-out generalization behaviors.
record.test_reason: The study reports held-out Adam and SGD performance on CIFAR10/100, bearing on V4, and a batch-size sweep with a common training budget, bearing on V5. The record overlooks the latter experiment.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that critical-momentum augmentation promotes exploration toward flatter regions and improves performance across supervised and online-learning benchmarks. Their SGD experiments show similar validation accuracy with reported early-training speed-ups from memory augmentation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses optimizer comparisons and validation performance on image-classification benchmarks, but does not reproduce Wilson et al.'s benchmark suite or its limited-learning-rate-and-decay-schedule tuning comparison. The Adam and SGD results are presented in separate tables.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that batch size and buffer size affect Adam+CM validation accuracy on CIFAR10/100; batch size 64 and buffer size 5 work best among the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam+CM lowers maximum-Hessian-eigenvalue sharpness and unscaled m-sharpness; buffer size and learning rate also alter sharpness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer and hyperparameter choices change unscaled sharpness, which need not rank validation accuracy monotonically. These measurements do not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam+CM and its SAM variant improve several supervised and online-learning validation results relative to Adam-based baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Critical-momentum augmentation can improve Adam's held-out performance; comparisons among Adam variants alone do not establish an adaptive-versus-SGD advantage or disadvantage.

record.problems: Adam and SGD validation results appear in separate tables and sections, so the comparison is not shown under a single matched experimental presentation. The paper reports five-seed averages but does not provide a direct Adam-versus-SGD statistical comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results omitted. Sharpness, buffer variance, cosine similarity, and parameter-distance measurements do not measure the training–test gap named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and learned local connectivity.

A documented matched comparison restricted to learning-rate and schedule tuning; equal training performance; changes from limited to broader tuning; switching optimizers; decoupled-weight-decay interventions; adaptive-versus-SGD language-model comparisons.
Longer training and interventions using warmup, learning-rate scaling, normalization or regularization; language-model batch-size comparisons.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus measured training–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, including comparisons with norm and margin measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: Add batch-size comparison rows for ResNet34 trained with Adam+CM on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100: batch sizes 128, 256 and 512 against 64, using best validation accuracy after hyperparameter searches. The text explicitly identifies 64 as best on both datasets; exact bar values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.
missing.locator: Section 5.2, Figure 10 left; 100-epoch training protocol earlier in Section 5.2

record.verdict_notes: Separate tables do not by themselves invalidate the Adam–SGD comparison; incomplete documentation of SGD tuning is the substantive limitation. The numerical reversals do not refute V4's qualified statement that adaptive methods often perform worse. The supplied text suffices for the qualitative V5 result, but not exact Figure 10 values.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.

The paper does not report a direct Adam-versus-SGD comparison in the same table or setup, language benchmarks comparing adaptive methods with SGD, or whether broader tuning removes or reverses differences.
Large-batch versus small-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout interventions and their held-out error effects.
Whether magnitude-aware sharpness tracks the training–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.
